subject: Unable to estimate after moving parameters to transformed_parameters block

messages.author: cf47bbe63da1f3ae
messages.subject: Unable to estimate after moving parameters to transformed_parameters block
parts:
I am trying to write a function to allow a simple specification and estimation of a variety of heirarchical multivariate time series models.
I can estimate a general variant of the model just fine, when the temporal structure (DRIFT matrix) is generated in the parameters block. In order to estimate more specific / complicated models I need to be able to specify the value of certain DRIFT parameters, but when I move this matrix to the transformed_parameters block, without changing anything else, the model no longer estimates, but I get a bunch of:

Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected because of the following issue:
stan::prob::normal_log(N4stan5agrad3varE): Random variable is 1.#QNAN:0, but must not be nan!

then sampling is not done.

I set relatively informative priors on the parameters, though no hard constraints. This seems to occur whichever matrix I move into transformed_parameters - I really need all of them there. I hope it's just something simple I am misunderstanding.

Attached is some example data and a working and failing script for rstan.

Cheers for any help!

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Unable to estimate after moving parameters to transformed_parameters block
parts:
On Monday, July 13, 2015 at 6:52:10 AM UTC-4, Charles Driver wrote:
Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected because of the following issue: stan::prob::normal_log(N4stan5agrad3varE): Random variable is 1.#QNAN:0, but must not be nan!

You have declared in transformed parameters

matrix[nlatent,nlatent] DRIFT[nsubjects];

but then DRIFT is not subsequently defined. Thus, its elements are initialized to NaN and when you then call

      for(driftcol in 1:nlatent){
        if(driftrow != driftcol) DRIFT[subjecti][driftrow,driftcol] ~ normal(0,1);
        if(driftrow == driftcol) DRIFT[subjecti][driftrow,driftcol] ~ normal(0.5,.5);

you get that error message. So, you have to define the elements of DRIFT, at which point you should not ignore the Jacobian warnings the parser gives you.

Ben

messages.subject: Re: Unable to estimate after moving parameters to transformed_parameters block
parts:
Thanks for this, I didn't realise transformed parameters all had to be specified - I'm getting sensible results now.

 Regarding the jacobian warnings though - do I really need to worry about them if I am just taking single parameters or data values and placing them in a matrix?

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Unable to estimate after moving parameters to transformed_parameters block
parts:
On Monday, July 20, 2015 at 6:04:39 PM UTC-4, Charles Driver wrote:
Thanks for this, I didn't realise transformed parameters all had to be specified - I'm getting sensible results now.
The transformed parameters block is for conditionally deterministic functions of the things in the parameters block. I'm not sure what you were expecting to happen if one were undefined.
Regarding the jacobian warnings though - do I really need to worry about them if I am just taking single parameters or data values and placing them in a matrix?

For identity "transformtions", the Jacobian determinant is just 1, so excluding it would not affect the posterior kernel.

Ben
